Class JsonValue

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.net.http.JsonValue
public final class JsonValue extends Object
One value inside a JSON document, with the navigation and conversion methods of JDK 28's JsonValue (JEP 540): get(String), get(int), asInt(), asString(), toString(). A value is the document plus the index where it starts: it never copies the document or parses it into a tree. Json.parse(String) validates the whole document once, so each later step only scans the value it starts from. 
JsonValue puzzle = Json.parse(response.body()).get("puzzle");
int rating = puzzle.get("rating").asInt();
JsonValue solution = puzzle.get("solution");
for (int i = 0; i < solution.size(); i++) {
    int length = solution.get(i).copyString(uci);
}

Unlike JEP 540 nothing throws: a missing member, an index out of range, a step into a non-container or an invalid document gives a value whose type() says so, every later step keeps that answer, and the as* conversions return zero values or null. As in JEP 540, asInt() and asLong() accept any integral number (123, 123.0, 2.3E2) and reject a fraction or an overflow.

Each get returns a new value, one 20-byte arena object that the collector reclaims; keep a value in a local variable rather than repeating a step. A value reads the document where it is, so a byte[] buffer must not be reused for another document while its values are still read.

    • copyString

      public int copyString(byte[] out)
      Decodes a JSON string, escapes included, to UTF-8 in out and returns the number of bytes written; 0 when this is not a string. Writes at most out.length bytes, never part of a character, and no NUL.
